name: Mark Warner
committees: Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs
stance: Flagship advocate for enforceable, testable AI safety and security standards — pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity, mandatory reporting of serious AI incidents, and keeping powerful systems under human control.

statements.text: Introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 with Sens. Schatz and Kim, setting enforceable safety and security standards for the most advanced AI — pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity, and mandatory reporting of serious AI safety and security incidents — and sought its passage on the Senate floor.
Unveiled six AI bills as part of a comprehensive AI legislative framework covering national security, job displacement and data centers.
AI has tremendous potential — but even the companies building it are sounding the alarm on the risks. Congress can’t afford to sit on the sidelines.
We cannot wait for AI companies to self-regulate. They are raising every alarm. Congress must act this week to meet the rapidly developing threat landscape posed by AI.
When AI leaders are saying with one voice that we need to slow down, we need to slow down.
NEW: OpenAI just came forward with six new incidents of “concerning” behavior by their AI models… including cases where the model inserted instructions to disregard its own constraints.
AI could take down entire banks or local water systems.
President Trump is fighting AI regulation while his own financial interests are increasingly tied to the industry.
AI security is the issue of our lifetimes. I will NOT stand by and wait for a catastrophe to happen — I’m fighting to pass basic safety legislation TODAY.
We cannot wait any longer. We must take action to put some guardrails on this tech before something catastrophic happens.
Forced a Senate vote on his AI guardrails legislation, which was blocked; said he would keep seeking bipartisan testing, incident reporting and safety requirements for AI systems.
Nobody would climb on an airplane that hadn’t been tested. Why are we letting rapidly accelerating AI models get rolled out left and right?
AI is already at a point where it could make serious attacks on our hospitals, banks, and water systems.

Artificial intelligence is one of the defining national security challenges of our time, and I welcome the administration recognizing that this technology requires serious, sustained attention at the highest levels of government.
establishing rigorous testing and safeguards so that increasingly powerful systems remain secure, reliable, and under human control.

AI is one of the defining national security challenges of our time. Naming a new “Super Intelligence Force” is not a substitute for a real AI strategy. We need clear safeguards, rigorous testing of our most advanced systems, and a coordinated approach to keeping America ahead of China and other adversaries.

When consumer AI agents are accessing YOUR bank account or using YOUR credit card, they must be subject to fiduciary-like duties of care. We need to pass my AI AGENTS Act to get some basic guardrails in place.
AI is already at a point where rogue agents are accessing Americans’ bank accounts. Standing by is not an option.
